entries.summary: Amanda VanDerHeyden's keynote on lessons learned from 15 years of multi-tiered systems of support, hosted by Branching Minds. Useful for leaders reviewing their own MTSS.

entries.title: Morphology and spelling, with Lyn Stone
entries.by: The Reading League Illinois, with Lyn Stone
entries.summary: Lyn Stone presents on morphology and spelling for The Reading League Illinois. A long session for teachers wanting to deepen their knowledge of how words are built.

entries.title: Learning through and to talk: why oracy matters, with Voice 21
entries.by: Education Scotland, with Voice 21
entries.summary: Voice 21 presents on why oracy matters, learning both through talk and to talk, in a session hosted by Education Scotland. Useful for teachers planning how talk is taught.

entries.title: Science of Reading Presentation by Pamela Snow
entries.by: Catholic Education Canberra Goulburn, with Pamela Snow
entries.summary: Professor Pamela Snow presents on the science of reading, in a session recorded for Catholic Education Canberra Goulburn's Catalyst program.

entries.title: Reading instruction in Australian schools: Headwinds, tailwinds and crosswinds
entries.by: Mornington Peninsula Foundation, with Pamela Snow
entries.summary: Pamela Snow's 2025 La Trobe Oration asks why reading instruction is still contested after decades of research, what has slowed research reaching classrooms, and what needs to change in teacher education.

entries.title: Oral language development and reading, with Professor Pamela Snow
entries.by: Spellcaster Education, with Pamela Snow
entries.summary: Professor Pamela Snow speaks about oral language development and its relationship to reading, in a session hosted by Spellcaster Education.

entries.title: Stephanie Le Lievre: A knowledge-based comprehension model
entries.by: Read Ballarat, with Stephanie Le Lievre
entries.summary: Stephanie Le Lievre presents a knowledge-based model of reading comprehension in a session for Read Ballarat. Useful for teachers rethinking how comprehension is taught.

entries.title: Dr Kate Jacobs: Specific learning disorders (SLDs)
entries.by: Learning Difficulties Australia, with Kate Jacobs
entries.summary: A Learning Difficulties Australia session with Dr Kate Jacobs on specific learning disorders. A possible starting point before looking at each disorder in turn.

entries.title: Sarah Asome: Response to intervention
entries.by: Learning Difficulties Australia, with Sarah Asome
entries.summary: Victorian school leader Sarah Asome presents on response to intervention for Learning Difficulties Australia. Useful for teams building or reviewing their own tiers of support.

entries.title: Dr Kate de Bruin: Using universal design principles to support every student
entries.by: Learning Difficulties Australia, with Kate de Bruin
entries.summary: Inclusive education researcher Dr Kate de Bruin presents for Learning Difficulties Australia on using universal design principles to support every student.

entries.title: Understanding DLD: Developmental language disorder, with Tiffany Hogan
entries.by: Reading Universe, with Tiffany Hogan
entries.summary: Researcher Tiffany Hogan on developmental language disorder, in a session for Reading Universe. A manageable length for teachers who are new to the topic.
staff: Which of our students read words accurately but still struggle to understand spoken and written language?
How do we share concerns about a student's language with our speech pathologist or the family?

entries.title: Understanding developmental language disorder (DLD) and dysgraphia
entries.by: Speech Pathology Tasmania
entries.summary: A session from Speech Pathology Tasmania on understanding developmental language disorder and dysgraphia together, from an Australian speech pathology point of view.

entries.title: Dyslexia and language: Disorder or difference? Maggie Snowling
entries.by: Gresham College, with Maggie Snowling
entries.summary: Professor Maggie Snowling's Gresham College lecture on dyslexia and language. An hour-long public lecture from a leading dyslexia researcher.
staff: What do we currently believe causes dyslexia, and where did those beliefs come from?
How well do we look at oral language when a student is struggling to read?

entries.title: Dyslexia and developmental language disorder, with Dr Tiffany Hogan
entries.by: Learning MATTERS, with Tiffany Hogan
entries.summary: Dr Tiffany Hogan joins New Zealand's Learning MATTERS for a session on dyslexia and developmental language disorder together.

entries.title: Why are children who struggle with reading at higher risk of emotional problems?
entries.by: Macquarie University Centre for Reading
entries.summary: A Macquarie University Centre for Reading seminar asking why children who struggle with reading are more likely to have emotional difficulties. A reminder to watch wellbeing alongside intervention.

entries.title: Reading the Room: Explaining the International Dyslexia Association's new definition of dyslexia
entries.by: National Center on Improving Literacy
entries.summary: A National Center on Improving Literacy session explaining the International Dyslexia Association's updated definition of dyslexia. Good for leaders who need to keep school documents current.

entries.title: Early identification of dyslexia: Research to practice, with Dr Hugh Catts
entries.by: The Windward Institute, with Hugh Catts
entries.summary: Researcher Hugh Catts presents for the Windward Institute on identifying dyslexia early. Relevant to Foundation and Year 1 teams and anyone responsible for screening.

entries.title: Inside a dyslexia intervention: Reading strategies for struggling readers
entries.by: Understood
entries.summary: Understood's video takes you inside a dyslexia intervention session. Handy for staff who have never watched specialist reading intervention being taught.

entries.title: Dyslexia myths, misconceptions and facts, with Tim Odegard
entries.by: Speaking of Psychology (American Psychological Association), with Tim Odegard
entries.summary: The American Psychological Association's podcast Speaking of Psychology talks with researcher Tim Odegard about myths, misconceptions and facts about dyslexia. This is the video recording of the episode.

entries.title: Dyslexia and dysgraphia webinar
entries.by: Lyn Stone
entries.summary: A webinar from Australian linguist Lyn Stone, made for parents who want to know more about dyslexia and dysgraphia. Clear enough for teachers too, and one to pass on to families.

entries.title: Robyn Bartram: The handwriting expert
entries.by: Learning Difficulties Australia, with Robyn Bartram
entries.summary: Robyn Bartram presents on handwriting for Learning Difficulties Australia. One for junior teams reviewing how handwriting is taught and supported.

entries.title: Alison Clarke: Spelling
entries.by: Learning Difficulties Australia, with Alison Clarke
entries.summary: Melbourne speech pathologist Alison Clarke presents on spelling for Learning Difficulties Australia. Relevant to anyone supporting students whose spelling lags behind their reading.

entries.title: Dr Alison Madelaine: Rethinking Tier 1 spelling instruction
entries.by: Five from Five, with Alison Madelaine
entries.summary: Dr Alison Madelaine's guest presentation for Five from Five on rethinking classroom spelling teaching. Strong Tier 1 spelling is the first support for students with written expression difficulties.

strand: The Writing Rope and views of writing
entries.title: Steve Graham: An overview of effective K to 12 writing instruction, from handwriting to writing genres
entries.by: The Reading League Vermont, with Steve Graham
entries.summary: Writing researcher Steve Graham gives The Reading League Vermont an overview of effective writing teaching, from handwriting through to genres.

entries.title: Evidence-based handwriting instruction and assessment webinar
entries.by: Iowa Reading Research Center
entries.summary: An Iowa Reading Research Center webinar on teaching and assessing handwriting using evidence. Helpful for schools without an agreed way to check handwriting fluency.

strand: The Writing Rope and views of writing
entries.title: Steve Graham: Effective writing instruction
entries.by: Reading Rockets, with Steve Graham
entries.summary: A Reading Rockets video with writing researcher Steve Graham on effective writing teaching. Pairs well with the Karen Harris podcast episode on self-regulated strategy development on the Listen shelf.

entries.title: Why is teaching handwriting so difficult and what can we do about it?
entries.by: Thinking Deeply about Primary Education
entries.summary: An episode of the UK podcast Thinking Deeply about Primary Education on why handwriting is hard to teach well and what teachers can do about it. This is the video recording of the episode.

entries.title: Steve Chinn: How to teach maths, understanding learners' needs
entries.by: The Dyscalculia Network, with Steve Chinn
entries.summary: Rob Jennings of The Dyscalculia Network interviews Steve Chinn, a long-standing UK specialist in maths learning difficulties, about his book on teaching maths with learners' needs in mind.

entries.title: Understanding dyscalculia
entries.by: Education Scotland
entries.summary: Education Scotland's webinar on understanding dyscalculia. A full session for maths leaders and intervention staff.

entries.title: Understanding developmental dyscalculia: A math learning disability (webinar)
entries.by: LD@school, with Daniel Ansari
entries.summary: Professor Daniel Ansari's webinar for Canada's LD@school explains developmental dyscalculia, a specific learning disability affecting maths in about five per cent of children. The page includes a transcript.
staff: Which early number skills do we check in Foundation and Year 1?
What would we want a parent to hear from us if we suspected a persistent maths difficulty?

entries.title: Count Me In! Supporting students in your class with math difficulty
entries.by: National Center on Intensive Intervention
entries.summary: Dr Sarah Powell walks through free tools from the National Center on Intensive Intervention for assessing and teaching students with maths difficulty.

entries.title: Intensive intervention in mathematics: Course content
entries.by: National Center on Intensive Intervention
entries.summary: Eight free training modules from the National Center on Intensive Intervention on delivering intensive maths intervention and adjusting it using student data. Suited to interventionists and maths leaders.

entries.title: Joni Holmes: Working memory and classroom learning
entries.by: Cambridge University Press ELT, with Joni Holmes
entries.summary: Researcher Joni Holmes speaks on working memory and classroom learning. Relevant across this section, because many students with learning difficulties also find it hard to hold information in mind.

entries.title: Developmental coordination disorder: Professor Amanda Kirby
entries.by: Association for Child and Adolescent Mental Health, with Amanda Kirby
entries.summary: Professor Amanda Kirby speaks for the Association for Child and Adolescent Mental Health about developmental coordination disorder, which often shows up at school in handwriting and organisation. Made for clinicians, so heavier going than the short video in this strand.

entries.title: Understanding ADHD in children and how to support them at school
entries.by: Wolfson Centre for Young People's Mental Health, with Joanna Martin
entries.summary: Dr Joanna Martin of Cardiff University on the early signs of ADHD in primary school children, how it can look different in girls and boys, what to do when you have concerns and how schools can help.

entries.title: Why rewards don't always stick: Understanding ADHD and motivation, with Rebecca McLinden
entries.by: ADHD Australia, with Rebecca McLinden
entries.summary: Behaviour analyst Rebecca McLinden, speaking for ADHD Australia, on how ADHD affects the way rewards work, and why motivation and consistency can be hard to keep up.

entries.title: ADHD and co-occurring autism, with Monique Mitchelson
entries.by: ADHD Australia, with Monique Mitchelson
entries.summary: Monique Mitchelson's talk for ADHD Australia's Global ADHD Conference on ADHD and co-occurring autism. Helpful background when a student's profile does not fit one label neatly.

entries.title: ADHD goes to school: Webinar recording
entries.by: Kelty Mental Health Resource Centre
entries.summary: A webinar for parents from Canada's Kelty Mental Health Resource Centre on how ADHD affects learning and how to support a child at school. Useful for seeing school through a family's eyes. Some of the advice is specific to British Columbia.

entries.title: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in children and teenagers: Webinar recording
entries.by: Raising Children Network
entries.summary: A recorded webinar on ADHD in children and teenagers from the Raising Children Network, the Australian parenting website. Worth knowing about when a family asks you where to start.

entries.title: inclusionED The Inclusive Classroom, Episode 1: Neurodiversity in the classroom
entries.by: inclusionED (Sylvia Rodger Institute)
entries.summary: The first episode of inclusionED's webinar series The Inclusive Classroom. It introduces neurodiversity and autism and offers classroom strategies, from sensory needs to building on students' strengths and interests.
staff: What do we already do at Tier 1 that helps autistic students and everyone else?
Which one strategy from this session could every classroom adopt this term?

entries.title: inclusionED The Inclusive Classroom, Episode 3: Sensory needs
entries.by: inclusionED (Sylvia Rodger Institute)
entries.summary: The third episode of inclusionED's webinar series explains sensory seeking and sensory avoiding, and how being more or less sensitive to what is going on in a classroom affects students.

entries.title: Supporting autistic girls at school: Full video
entries.by: Yellow Ladybugs, with the Victorian Government
entries.summary: A recorded panel from Yellow Ladybugs and the Victorian Government. Panellists share their own experience of six areas that often challenge autistic girls at school, including hidden anxiety, peer relationships and class rules.

entries.title: Executive functioning: Webinar recording and resources
entries.by: Positive Partnerships
entries.summary: A recorded webinar on planning, shifting attention, flexible thinking and self-regulation in young autistic people, with slides, a strategy list for home and school and a planning template.

entries.title: Communication and autism: Two webinar recordings and resources
entries.by: Positive Partnerships
entries.summary: Two recorded webinars on the different ways autistic people communicate, being a good communication partner and extending two-way interaction, with slides and a planning tool.

entries.title: Making Sense of Autism (shortened version)
entries.by: Autism Education Trust
entries.summary: A shortened version of the Autism Education Trust's Making Sense of Autism training, made to help education staff understand autism better, with ideas for support in the classroom and at home.

entries.title: Dysregulation: Supporting autistic people, families and educators (A Different Brilliant, S6 Ep6)
entries.by: Aspect (Autism Spectrum Australia)
entries.summary: An episode of Aspect's podcast A Different Brilliant on what dysregulation is, what can contribute to it and how adults can support an autistic person who is overwhelmed. This is the video recording of the episode.

entries.title: Unpacking the effective use of teaching assistants
entries.by: Evidence for Learning
entries.summary: An Evidence for Learning webinar with practical, evidence-based advice on getting the most from teaching assistants in primary and secondary schools. It builds on Evidence for Learning's guidance report on the same topic.
staff: When are our education support staff working with the students who most need the teacher?
What preparation and feedback time do teachers and support staff have together each week?

entries.title: How to support neurodiversity and disability inclusion in school communities
entries.by: Be You (Beyond Blue)
entries.summary: A recorded Be You session on how to support neurodiversity and disability inclusion in school communities. Be You is the national mental health in education initiative led by Beyond Blue.

entries.title: Multi-tiered system of supports in schools, Part 1: A rationale for change
entries.by: Kate de Bruin
entries.summary: Dr Kate de Bruin's short presentation, recorded for the ACT Inclusive Education Community of Practice, on why schools should move to a multi-tiered system of supports.

entries.title: inclusionED The Inclusive Classroom, Episode 4: Foundation practices for early career teachers
entries.by: inclusionED (Sylvia Rodger Institute)
entries.summary: The fourth episode of inclusionED's webinar series, on foundation practices for early career teachers. It also introduces the professional learning and community of practice on the inclusionED website.

entries.title: Professor Linda Graham on inclusive education (The School Can't Experience Podcast, episode 50)
entries.by: The School Can't Experience Podcast, with Linda Graham
entries.summary: Professor Linda Graham, Director of the QUT Centre for Inclusive Education, talks with host Leisa Reichelt about teaching and assessment that every student can access, and what the Disability Standards ask of schools. This is the video recording of the podcast episode.

entries.title: Dr Wes Hoover explains the Simple View of Reading
entries.by: The Reading League, with Wesley Hoover
entries.summary: Wesley Hoover explains the Simple View of Reading in under three minutes, in a short video from The Reading League's Defining Guide series.
staff: Which of our students decode well but understand little, and which understand well when listening but struggle to decode?
How do our assessments tell us whether decoding or language comprehension is holding a student back?

entries.title: The Simple View and Scarborough's Reading Rope, with Hugh Catts
entries.by: Melissa and Lori Love Literacy, with Hugh Catts
entries.summary: Reading researcher Hugh Catts joins the Melissa and Lori Love Literacy podcast to talk about the Simple View of Reading and Scarborough's Reading Rope. This is the video of episode 178.
staff: Which strands of the Reading Rope get the most teaching time in our school, and which get the least?
What would change in our planning if word recognition and language comprehension were both everyone's job from Foundation to Year 6?

entries.title: Q and A with Hollis Scarborough
entries.by: SoR: What I Should Have Learned in College, with Hollis Scarborough
entries.summary: A question and answer session with Hollis Scarborough, the researcher who created the Reading Rope. It runs for a little over an hour.

entries.title: Building the language house
entries.by: Spelfabet
entries.summary: A short video on building the language house from Spelfabet, the site run by Australian speech pathologist Alison Clarke. It runs for about nine minutes.

entries.title: SOLAR: Science of Language and Reading, with Pamela Snow
entries.by: Teaching Literacy Podcast, with Pamela Snow
entries.summary: Pamela Snow joins the Teaching Literacy Podcast to talk about SOLAR, the Science of Language and Reading, the framework her Language House illustrates. This is the video of episode 21.

entries.title: What is the Writing Rope?
entries.by: Reading Universe
entries.summary: A short Reading Universe video that answers the question in its title. At under ten minutes, it is a quick way to introduce the Writing Rope to a team.
staff: Which strands of the Writing Rope do we teach explicitly, and which do we mostly leave to chance?
Where do handwriting and spelling still hold our writers back, and what would it take to make them automatic?
entries.strand: The Writing Rope and views of writing

entries.title: Teaching children to write well, with Joan Sedita
entries.by: Reading Universe, with Joan Sedita
entries.summary: Joan Sedita, founder of Keys to Literacy, presents her Writing Rope and shows how thinking, language, structure and craft weave together, using real student work and classroom video.
entries.strand: The Writing Rope and views of writing

entries.title: The Writing Rope and integrating reading and writing, with Joan Sedita
entries.by: The Reading League Florida, with Joan Sedita
entries.summary: Joan Sedita presents for The Reading League Florida on the Writing Rope and on integrating reading and writing instruction.
entries.strand: The Writing Rope and views of writing

entries.title: The Writing Rope: Five-part webinar series with Joan Sedita
entries.by: PaTTAN, with Joan Sedita
entries.summary: A PaTTAN playlist of five sessions on the Writing Rope. The first introduces the rope and what is known about effective writing instruction, and it suits a team working through the framework over a term.
entries.strand: The Writing Rope and views of writing

entries.title: The Not So Simple View of Writing: Is it really that simple?
entries.by: MiMTSS Technical Assistance Center
entries.summary: A session from the MiMTSS Technical Assistance Center on the Not So Simple View of Writing. It runs for about 80 minutes, and the presenter is not named in the title.
entries.strand: The Writing Rope and views of writing

entries.title: Interview with Dr Linnea Ehri (The Reading League Podcast, episode 11)
entries.by: The Reading League, with Linnea Ehri
entries.summary: A long-form interview with reading researcher Linnea Ehri, from The Reading League's podcast Teaching, Reading and Learning.

entries.title: Orthographic mapping: What it is and why it's so important
entries.by: The Reading League, with Maria Murray
entries.summary: Maria Murray of The Reading League explains what orthographic mapping is and why it is so important, in a talk of about 35 minutes.

entries.title: Orthographic mapping explainer
entries.by: Lyn Stone
entries.summary: Australian educational linguist Lyn Stone gives a short explainer on orthographic mapping. A quick starting point before the longer talks.

entries.title: Professor Anne Castles: Teaching sight words
entries.by: Learning Difficulties Australia, with Anne Castles
entries.summary: Anne Castles, co-author of Ending the Reading Wars, presents for Learning Difficulties Australia on teaching sight words.

entries.title: How the brain learns to read: Professor Stanislas Dehaene
entries.by: WISE Channel, with Stanislas Dehaene
entries.summary: Professor Stanislas Dehaene's lecture on how the brain learns to read, published by the WISE Channel and about 34 minutes long.

entries.title: An interview with Dr Louisa Moats: Revisiting Teaching Reading Is Rocket Science 2020
entries.by: PaTTAN, with Louisa Moats
entries.summary: Louisa Moats talks with PaTTAN about the 2020 edition of Teaching Reading Is Rocket Science. It pairs well with reading the paper itself, which is also in this section.

entries.title: Ending the reading wars: Kathy Rastle
entries.by: Psychology at the University of Edinburgh, with Kathleen Rastle
entries.summary: Kathleen Rastle, co-author of Ending the Reading Wars, gives a lecture of the same name, shared by Psychology at the University of Edinburgh.

entries.title: A matter of translation: researchED Brisbane keynote, with Professor Tanya Serry
entries.by: A Learner's Toolkit, with Tanya Serry
entries.summary: Professor Tanya Serry's keynote at researchED Brisbane in 2025, titled A matter of translation and shared on the A Learner's Toolkit channel.

entries.title: Pamela Snow: Effective literacy instruction is essential to overcoming disadvantage
entries.by: Knowledge Society, with Pamela Snow
entries.summary: Pamela Snow, in a short talk for Knowledge Society, on why effective literacy instruction is essential to overcoming disadvantage.

entries.title: Leaders and learning in literacy: Structured literacy, with Dr Louise Spear-Swerling
entries.by: PaTTAN, with Louise Spear-Swerling
entries.summary: Louise Spear-Swerling talks with PaTTAN about structured literacy, in a session from its Leaders and Learning in Literacy series.

entries.title: Teaching content is teaching reading
entries.by: Daniel Willingham
entries.summary: Daniel Willingham's ten-minute video making the case that teaching content is teaching reading. Short enough to show in a staff meeting.

entries.title: Rethinking reading comprehension, with researcher Hugh Catts
entries.by: Melissa and Lori Love Literacy, with Hugh Catts
entries.summary: Hugh Catts joins the Melissa and Lori Love Literacy podcast to talk about rethinking reading comprehension. This is the video of episode 118, and it pairs with his American Educator article.

entries.title: Pamela Snow on early language and literacy skills
entries.by: Progressively Incorrect (Zach Groshell), with Pamela Snow
entries.summary: Pamela Snow talks with Zach Groshell about early language and literacy skills, in an hour-long episode of his podcast.

entries.title: Dr Keith Stanovich: Matthew effects, does reading make you smarter?
entries.by: Children of the Code, with Keith Stanovich
entries.summary: Keith Stanovich talks about Matthew effects in reading and whether reading makes you smarter, in a six-minute interview clip from the Children of the Code project.

entries.title: Dr Tessa Daffern: Assessment-informed practices in teaching spelling
entries.by: Learning Difficulties Australia, with Tessa Daffern
entries.summary: Tessa Daffern presents for Learning Difficulties Australia on using assessment to guide the teaching of spelling.

entries.title: Susan Brady: Phoneme awareness: What we now know
entries.by: Oregon RTIi, with Susan Brady
entries.summary: Susan Brady presents on phoneme awareness and what is now known about it, in a session of about 75 minutes shared by Oregon RTIi.

entries.title: Is handwriting actually important for writing?
entries.by: Reading Universe, with Joan Sedita
entries.summary: Joan Sedita explains in two minutes why effortful handwriting takes energy away from composing, and why handwriting letters while learning their sounds helps young students.
